author: cli
text:
Re-read at 0.57.2. The comments in this parser still describe it; the rot flag fired because visit_Call's emission gained a field.

New at module-parser level: PythonParser declares builtin_names, DERIVED from dir(builtins) rather than typed out - the interpreter is the source of what shadows a repo name, and lesson 11 says pin the derivation, not the list. edges.py reads it off the parser for the CALLER's extension, so the language fact lives with whoever knows the grammar.

Measured consequence: sqlalchemy declares Options.isinstance, Row.tuple and BaseRow.getattr as methods, and bare builtin calls were resolving to them - 1,150, 185 and 367 edges respectively.

text: Re-read at the literal-receiver change. Comments verified and unchanged. This parser now emits literal_recv via the module-level helper _py_literal_recv; `import ast` moved to module scope to support it. See _unreachable_target for why.

author: cli
text:
Re-read at the unparsed-file fix. Comments verified and unchanged.

ONE LINE CHANGED AND IT WAS THE IMPORTANT ONE: `except SyntaxError: return [], []` now raises. Returning an empty pair says 'this file contains nothing', which is indistinguishable from an empty file - so a file with a syntax error indexed as zero entities, verify-change reported 'no entity-level changes detected', and --gate exited 0 on a change whose impact had never been computed.

The indexer already wrapped parse() and recorded what it caught; it simply never had anything to catch. PARSE_SCHEMA_VERSION 11 -> 12, because a cache warmed at 11 holds the empty result for a broken file and would replay exactly the silence this removes.
